verdict.reasoning: The sole paper, [MASK] is All You Need, proposes Discrete Interpolants that share parameters across two conditional directions (image↔mask) for pre-specified modalities. However, the gap calls for modeling *all* conditional distributions p(x_S | x_not_S) for *arbitrary* subsets S of variables — a combinatorial set well beyond two paired modalities. The paper does not address arbitrary subset conditioning, handling only fixed modality pairs. While it demonstrates shared-parameter conditioning in a limited setting, it does not tackle the core problem of the gap, so the gap remains open.

paper.title: [MASK] is All You Need
paper.abstract: In generative models, two paradigms have gained attraction in various applications: next-set prediction-based Masked Generative Models and next-noise prediction-based Non-Autoregressive Models, e.g., Diffusion Models. In this work, we propose using discrete-state models to connect them and explore their scalability in the vision domain. First, we conduct a step-by-step analysis in a unified design space across two types of models including timestep-independence, noise schedule, temperature, guidance strength, etc in a scalable manner. Second, we re-cast typical discriminative tasks, e.g., image segmentation, as an unmasking process from [MASK] tokens on a discrete-state model. This enables us to perform various sampling processes, including flexible conditional sampling by only training once to model the joint distribution. All aforementioned explorations lead to our framework named Discrete Interpolants, which enables us to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance compared to previous discrete-state based methods in various benchmarks, like ImageNet256, MS COCO, and video dataset FaceForensics. In summary, by leveraging [MASK] in discrete-state models, we can bridge Masked Generative and Non-autoregressive Diffusion models, as well as generative and discriminative tasks.

assessments.contribution_summary: The paper proposes Discrete Interpolants, a discrete-state generative modeling framework. It shows that by training a single model on the joint distribution of two modalities (e.g., image and segmentation mask), one can perform conditional sampling tasks such as image-conditioned mask generation and mask-conditioned image generation using classifier-free guidance. This demonstrates shared-parameter conditional modeling for specific pre-defined pairs of variables.
assessments.what_remains_open: The gap asks about modeling ALL conditional distributions p(x_S | x_not_S) for arbitrary subsets S of variables within a dataset. The paper only handles conditioning between two pre-specified modalities (or class-conditional generation). It does not address the general problem of arbitrary subset conditioning — e.g., conditioning on some pixels/features of an image to predict others, or handling more than two modalities with arbitrary conditioning patterns. The framework is limited to pre-defined paired modalities and does not extend to the full combinatorial set of all possible conditional distributions.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: High tractability. Data is abundant (any dataset from a joint distribution works), compute is modest (single GPU, standard model sizes), and there is a well-established methodological path: train a single model f(x, mask) on random masking patterns to predict the held-out variables — directly extending BERT-style masked modeling, MADE, or masked autoencoders to arbitrary subsets. The scope is focused (one model, one training objective), and evaluation is straightforward (conditional log-likelihood, sampling quality, consistency checks). The main open challenges are ensuring consistency across exponentially many conditioning sets and scaling to high-dimensional variables, but these are engineering/nuance problems rather than fundamental breakthroughs.
